Session: `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`

Container & model: M, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-②: no
Serial constraints cleared: co-dispatched **#6194** (`packages/plugin-form/**`) — disjoint. ⛔ Nothing in flight touches `.npmrc`.

## Unblocked — gate 1 is discharged, and here is the proof

`Blocked-by: #5306`. **#5306 landed this round** as PR #6311, squashed to `main` as `b1c1e3bfe` (*"fix(repo): declare the Node/pnpm floors the toolchain actually requires"*). Root `package.json` now reads:

```json
"engines": { "node": ">=22.11", "pnpm": ">=10" }
```

So the range this card would enforce is the corrected one, and the card's own Option-C warning — ⛔ *"enforcing the old lying range would block valid environments"* — no longer applies.

⚠️ Re-verify that on your own base before touching `.npmrc`. If `engines` does not read exactly the above, **stop**: something reverted or amended it and this card's premise is gone.

## Zone 1 — Ruling and the gate that remains (binding)

The maintainer approved Option C as this gated follow-up (2026-08-25, verbatim 「就全部接受，然后继续下一批」). ⭐ **Gate 2 is the work**, not a formality, and the card states it precisely:

> verify against the environments that would be refused: CI workflow images (every workflow that runs `pnpm install`), the documented contributor setup, and the remote-agent session images. Record the readings in this card; **if any live environment fails the corrected range, fixing THAT is a prerequisite, not a reason to widen the range back.**

⛔ That last clause is the one to hold onto. If something fails, the answer is **never** to loosen `engines` — that would undo #5306 and re-create the exact false declaration this family exists to remove. Fix the environment, or stop and report.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism readings (verify; and one of these I could not take)

- `.npmrc` on `origin/main` carries **only** `auto-install-peers=true` — no `engine-strict` anywhere. So this is an **addition**, not a value change.
- Every workflow uses `node-version: '22.x'`, which resolved to **22.23.2** in a CI job log read on #5306 — above the 22.11 floor. pnpm comes from `corepack enable` plus root `packageManager: pnpm@10.31.0`, i.e. 10.31.0 ≥ 10. Both look clean, but ⛔ **that is one job log from one workflow**, and the card asks for *every workflow that runs `pnpm install`*. Enumerate them and say which you checked.
- ⚠️ **The remote-agent session images are a reading I cannot take and neither may you be able to.** If you cannot enumerate or probe them, ⛔ do not silently drop that third population — say plainly that it is unverified and let the report carry the gap. An unverified third of the gate is a finding, not a rounding error.
- Node's own release cadence only moves `22.x` upward, so the CI half is stable in the safe direction. Contributor machines are not — that is the population this flag actually bites.

## ⭐ What "verify" has to mean here, because a green install proves less than it looks

`engine-strict` changes behaviour only for an environment **outside** the range. An install succeeding on a machine that already satisfies the floor tells you nothing about the flag. So the measurement that counts is the **refusal**: show that a node/pnpm combination below the floor is actually refused with the flag on, and that every environment you enumerated is above it. ⛔ A green `pnpm install` on the container you happen to be running in is not evidence.

## Blast radius, stated so you can weigh a stop

This flag refuses installs repo-wide. It lands on contributors and on other agent seats, not on you, and the failure appears at `pnpm install` — before any of this card's context is visible to whoever hit it. That asymmetry is why the card demands readings first. **If the readings are not clean, `needs_decision` with what you measured is the better delivery**, and it is not a failed run.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. A `.npmrc` change is install-time, so state whether `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` still succeeds with the flag on. Check for any test pinning `.npmrc` contents. Follow `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s own verdict; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label (#4912). Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe and quote each gate's verdict line.

⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`. ⛔ Do not touch root `package.json` — #5306 settled the range and it is not reopened here.

## Standing

Worktree-first before your first edit. Post **your own claim comment** with your branch — ⚠️ under `mode:subagent` your session ID is identical to mine (objectstack#12220), so the branch distinguishes it. Lead your report with the literal text `os-dev-report`, write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read it back after posting.

Expected outcome: `done` with a draft PR carrying `Fixes #6264`, **or** `needs_decision` with the readings if any enumerated environment fails the corrected range.

## Gate 2 readings (recorded here as the card requires)

Branch `claude/issue-6264-engine-strict`, final commit `34f337cb4`. Draft PR #6351 carries the same readings with full context.

### Gate 1 re-verified on my own base

Base `ed859aa35`; root `package.json` reads exactly `"engines": { "node": ">=22.11", "pnpm": ">=10" }`. Premise holds. Root `package.json` untouched.

### The refusal — measured, not assumed

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` against this repository, with a real below-floor node from `nvm install 22.4.0` and a real pnpm 9 from `npm install pnpm@9`:

| toolchain | engine-strict | exit | verdict line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| node 22.4.0 (below floor), pnpm 10.31.0 | on | 1 | `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE` — `Expected version: >=22.11` / `Got: v22.4.0` |
| node 22.4.0, pnpm 10.31.0 | off | 0 | `WARN Unsupported engine: wanted: {"node":">=22.11"}` |
| node 22.22.2, pnpm 9.15.9 (below floor) | on | 1 | `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE` — `Expected version: >=10` / `Got: 9.15.9` |
| node 22.22.2, pnpm 9.15.9 | off | 1 | `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE` — same |
| node 22.22.2, pnpm 10.31.0 (above both) | on | 0 | `Done in 2.5s using pnpm v10.31.0` |

⭐ **Two results worth the PM's attention.**

**(1) The flag's delta is the node axis only.** Rows 3 and 4 show `engines.pnpm` is *already* a hard failure today, flag or no flag — pnpm always refuses on its own version. So this change adds nothing on the pnpm axis; what it changes is `engines.node`, from a `WARN` to a refusal. The card's framing ("a contributor or agent on node 22.4 / pnpm 9 gets refused") is half already true.

**(2) A confound that nearly produced a false reading.** My first run showed the below-floor install *passing* with the flag on, which reads as "the flag does nothing". It was not. Because the manifest declares `packageManager`, pnpm re-execs itself and compares the node on `PATH`, not the node it was launched with — bisected to that single manifest field, and confirmed by a probe where pnpm reported `Got: v22.22.2` while running under 22.4.0. The corrected test puts 22.4.0 on `PATH` as the only node. Anyone re-verifying this should use PATH, not a launcher.

Cold-install evidence for dependency engines: the first install on this branch with the flag on installed all 1621 packages across 47 workspace projects, exit 0. No dependency's `engines` refuses at the current toolchain. A future dependency bump declaring a higher node floor would now hard-fail rather than warn.

### Population 1 — CI workflows: 12 install, all above the floor

A plain grep overcounts: four workflows only *discuss* `pnpm install` in comments (`doc-component-types`, `doc-fence-languages`, `pre-install-import-graph`, `half-state-patrol` are deliberately install-free). The real list, comment lines excluded:

`ci.yml` (6 jobs), `lint.yml`, `live-e2e.yml`, `node-esm-load-gate.yml`, `doc-snippet-types.yml`, `performance-budget.yml`, `published-dist-gate.yml`, `readme-exports.yml`, `shadcn-check.yml`, `spec-range-floors.yml`, `changeset-release.yml`.

Every one: `corepack enable`, `actions/setup-node@v7` with `node-version: '22.x'`, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. pnpm resolves through corepack against `packageManager: pnpm@10.31.0`, above the 10 floor.

`node-version: '22.x'` measured against `nodejs.org/dist/index.json` resolves to **v22.23.2** — independently reproducing the 22.23.2 you read in the #5306 job log. ⚠️ Note 13 of the 35 released 22.x versions are below 22.11, so "node 22" is not automatically above the floor; only "latest 22.x" is. `22.x` moves upward only, so this half is stable in the safe direction.

### Population 2 — documented contributor setup: matches exactly

`CONTRIBUTING.md` lines 23-24 already state Node.js 22.11 or higher and pnpm 10 or higher, each tied to the declaration it comes from. Nothing to fix, no prerequisite.

The "Node.js 20+" lines in `content/docs/guide/quick-start.md` and `building-crud-app.md` are outside this flag's radius — they describe building a reader's own app via `pnpm add @object-ui/*`, not installing this repo. Confirmed structurally: no publishable package declares `engines`, and there is no package-level `.npmrc`.

### Population 3 — remote-agent session images: UNVERIFIED

The container I built this in reads node **v22.22.2**, pnpm **10.31.0** — above both floors. ⛔ That is one image measured from the inside, **not the fleet**, and I am not dropping the distinction. Nothing in the repo would let the fleet be enumerated: no `.nvmrc`, no `.tool-versions`, no `devcontainer.json`, no `Dockerfile`, and no node version in `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.vscode/` or `.mcp.json`.

If any image in the fleet runs node below 22.11 with pnpm 10 or above, every seat on it breaks at `pnpm install` on merge, before any of this card's context is visible. Bounding it but not closing it: such an image is already emitting `WARN Unsupported engine` on every install today, and the pnpm axis already hard-fails today regardless of this flag.

### Verdict

No enumerated environment fails the corrected range, so nothing became a prerequisite and the range was **not** widened. The gate is satisfied for everything measurable and open on population 3 — a maintainer call, which is why PR #6351 is a draft.

## ACCEPT — PR #6351. ⛔ Held as draft: gate 2's third population is unverified, and that is the maintainer's to close.

`domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. Read against the diff and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report.

### ⭐ The confound it caught is the whole reason to trust the rest

The first below-floor run **passed with the flag on** — a reading whose obvious interpretation is *"the flag does nothing"*. It is not, and the dev did not accept it:

> Because the manifest declares `packageManager`, pnpm **re-execs** and compares the node on PATH rather than the node it was launched with.

Bisected to that single field, confirmed with a probe reporting `Got: v22.22.2` **while running under 22.4.0**, then re-tested with 22.4.0 as the only node on PATH — which refuses correctly. ⛔ Had that first green been reported as the measurement, this card would have landed a flag believed to enforce something it had never been shown to enforce, and the next person to doubt it would have found a passing test.

That is precisely the trap my order named — *"a green install proves almost nothing here"* — and it was not merely avoided, it was **explained**.

### The blast radius is measurably narrower than the card assumed

| axis | with the flag | without the flag |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **pnpm 9.15.9** | exit 1, `Expected version: >=10 / Got: 9.15.9` | exit 1, **same refusal** |
| **node 22.4.0** | exit 1, `Expected version: >=22.11 / Got: v22.4.0` | exit 0, `WARN Unsupported engine` |
| node 22.22.2 + pnpm 10.31.0 | exit 0, `Done in 2.5s` | — |

⭐ **pnpm always hard-fails on its own version, flag or no flag.** So this change adds nothing on the pnpm axis; its entire delta is `engines.node`, from a warning to a refusal. The card's stated scenario ("a contributor on node 22.4 **or pnpm 9**") is half already-enforced. That materially shrinks what the maintainer is being asked to accept, and it is the kind of correction that only comes from measuring both arms with a control.

Also worth keeping: `node-version: '22.x'` resolves to **v22.23.2** (independently reproducing the job-log reading from #5306), and **13 of 35 released 22.x versions are below 22.11** — so "node 22" is not automatically safe, which is the fact that makes this flag worth having at all.

### ⭐ It cleaned up a shared-container mutation its own test caused

`nvm` had set its **default alias** to the below-floor 22.4.0 — which would have handed node 22.4.0 to any other agent that sourced nvm in this container. It noticed, removed the alias, uninstalled 22.4.0, and restored the container to 22.22.2 / 10.31.0. Nobody asked for that. In a multi-agent container it is the difference between a test and a trap.

### The hold, and why it is not mine to lift

Gate 2 names three populations. Two are measured and clean. The third — **remote-agent session images** — is reported as **unverified, not passed**, exactly as my order demanded, with the reason: one sampled container is not the fleet, and the repo pins nothing that would enumerate it (no `.nvmrc`, no `.tool-versions`, no `devcontainer.json`, no `Dockerfile`).

⛔ I am not lifting that. Fleet shape is maintainer territory, and more practically **nobody on an agent seat can see the fleet** — including me. The PR stays **draft**, unarmed.

**Options, with the dev's recommendation and mine, which agree:**

- **B — hold until someone with fleet visibility confirms the session images clear the node floor, then merge unchanged.** Best if that visibility is cheap.
- **A — merge as-is, accepting a residual risk that is now bounded by measurement**: the only new refusal is node < 22.11 *with* pnpm ≥ 10, and any machine in that state is **already emitting `WARN Unsupported engine` on every install today**.
- **C — land a `.nvmrc` / `.tool-versions` pin** so the floor is self-serving for version-manager users. A good follow-up either way; ⛔ agreed that it should not be smuggled into this PR.
- **D — widen `engines` to fit the fleet.** ⛔ Rejected on sight: the card forbids it, and it would undo #5306 and re-create the false declaration this family exists to remove.

⚠️ If it goes to A and an image is below the floor, the failure lands on **other seats at `pnpm install`**, before any of this card's context is visible to whoever hits it. That asymmetry is the whole reason gate 2 exists.

### The two findings it could not file

⭐ It hit a real channel limitation — direct REST is 403 for its seat and the container's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a placeholder, and its contract forbids substituting the MCP endpoints for the mandated dedup search — so it **handed both over with the reason** rather than filing blind or dropping them. Correct on both counts.

- **`changelog.yml`'s merge driver runs `pnpm install` with no `corepack`/`setup-node`**, while both siblings configuring the identical driver do. Re-verified by me and filed as **#6358**, with the note that #5409 records that workflow as having 0 runs, so it may be latent.
- **The consumer-guide "Node.js 20+" claims** — ⛔ **already filed this round as #6307**, by the dev on #5306, with the extra measurement that the version-literal ledger cannot see the `**bold**` spelling. Not duplicated. Your dedup instinct was right; the card existed.
